actions.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 24 - 19.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

dimensions.assessment: Affects all federal agencies conducting rulemakings under 5 U.S.C. 553(c), individuals and groups submitting public comments, OMB, GSA, and GAO.
dimensions.evidence: the head of an agency shall verify, to the greatest extent possible, at the time the comment is submitted, whether the comment has been submitted by a human being.

dimensions.assessment: Changes how public comments are processed, verified, and displayed on electronic dockets by allowing agencies to publish single representative copies of mass comments instead of every identical submission.
dimensions.evidence: instead of making available through the electronic docket of the agency each comment identified as a mass comment under paragraph (2), the head of an agency may make available through such docket only a single representative sample

dimensions.assessment: Requires GSA to update Regulations.gov and shared eRulemaking systems and agencies to update websites, but does not specify funding levels.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator of General Services, acting through the eRulemaking Program Management Office, shall update Regulations.gov as necessary

dimensions.assessment: Amends section 206 of the E-Government Act of 2002 to create new government-wide regulatory management mandates, OMB guidance requirements, and agency policy duties.
dimensions.evidence: To amend section 206 of the E-Government Act of 2002 to improve the integrity and management of mass comments and computer-generated comments

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent procedural requirements on federal rulemaking and docket management systems.

missing_information: The cost of updating Regulations.gov and agency information systems.
Specific technological tools or vendors that will be used for human verification.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires federal agencies to verify human submission of comments, manage mass comments on electronic dockets, establish agency policies, and directs OMB, GSA, and GAO to issue guidance, update systems, and report on computer-generated comments.
